title: International and US state privacy laws (GDPR, UK GDPR, PIPEDA, Australia, CMIA/CCPA, Washington, Texas)
summary: Beyond HIPAA, other privacy laws may apply to mental health information depending on where the client and the clinician are. In the EU and the UK, health data is special category data under the GDPR and the UK GDPR. Canada splits privacy law between the federal PIPEDA and provincial health information laws. Australia's Privacy Act treats health information as sensitive information under the Australian Privacy Principles. In the US, state laws such as California's CMIA and CCPA, Washington's My Health My Data Act and Texas's medical records privacy law (shaped by HB 300) add duties beyond HIPAA, sometimes for apps and businesses that HIPAA does not reach. This page is information, not legal advice.
keyPoints: EU GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679): processing health data is prohibited unless an Article 9 condition applies, for example health or social care provided by or under a professional bound by secrecy, and the processing also needs an Article 6 lawful basis. Member States may add conditions for health data. The GDPR can reach providers outside the EU who offer services to people in the EU.

UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025: health data stays special category data. The ICO says all of the Act's data protection provisions were in force by June 2026 and has updated its special category guidance.

Canada: PIPEDA covers private-sector organizations in commercial activity, but several provinces have health information laws that apply instead of or alongside it, and public bodies follow separate laws. The Office of the Privacy Commissioner publishes which provincial laws are deemed substantially similar.

Australia: the Privacy Act 1988 and its 13 Australian Privacy Principles apply to health service providers, and health information is sensitive information with stricter rules. The Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 added a statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy and tiered penalties. Some states also have health records laws.

California CMIA (Civil Code section 56 and following) protects medical information held by providers and certain businesses. Since a 2022 amendment (AB 2089), a business offering a mental health digital service is treated as a provider under the CMIA. Information governed by the CMIA or HIPAA is largely exempt from the CCPA, while other sensitive personal information carries CCPA rights.

Washington's My Health My Data Act (chapter 19.373 RCW) protects consumer health data held by entities that HIPAA does not cover. It requires consent before collecting or sharing such data, restricts selling it, and is enforced by the Attorney General and by private lawsuits under the Consumer Protection Act.

Texas Health and Safety Code chapter 181 (expanded by HB 300 in 2011) uses a broader definition of covered entity than HIPAA, requires employee training on state and federal privacy law, and adds state penalties.
More US states are passing consumer health data laws, so check the law of the client's state as well as your own.
whatToDo: Identify where the client lives and where you and your vendors store or process data; more than one law may apply.
Use the right contract with each vendor: a BAA under HIPAA, a data processing agreement under the GDPR or UK GDPR, and equivalent terms elsewhere.
Keep only what you need, tell clients how their information is handled, and honor access and correction requests within the legal deadlines.
Before working with a client in another country, check that country's health privacy and professional rules.
Consult your regulator or licensing board, a data protection officer, or a lawyer licensed in the relevant jurisdiction.

appPositioning: The app keeps no client data, so most of these laws are not triggered by the app itself in Phases 1 to 3. If account data is ever stored (Phase 4), the spec calls for regional data residency and the right contracts with every vendor.

verification.note: No official site was loaded directly. EUR-Lex, legislation.gov.uk, ICO, OPC, OAIC, California AG, Washington AG and RCW, and Texas statutes pages were found through search results. The ICO's June 2026 commencement statement, the Australian 2024 amendments, CMIA's AB 2089 change and Washington's private right of action come from search snippets of official pages plus law-firm summaries. Sources disagree on which Canadian provincial health laws are deemed substantially similar, so none are named. Texas training timelines were not confirmed and are not stated.
